question: The 12-run study resumed a cache that was partly extracted before the September18 13:56 geometry fix. Are pre-fix cached rows consistent with post-fix code?

incident.fix_scope: Zero-area boundary candidates (e.g. [.978125,1.,1.,1.]) previously tripped the validator and aborted extraction. They are now preserved and yield zero context features. Candidates are not dropped or reordered.

evidence: Each cached file stores fingerprint=sha256(CONTRACT,row); the resume path re-verifies and raises Cache mismatch otherwise. The resumed pass completed all 134984 rows, so every pre-fix fingerprint matched the post-fix CONTRACT.
Failure mode was fail-closed: the pre-fix code raised rather than writing incorrect features.
Zero-area boxes were found only in post-fix files and always carry zero RoI features, the expected signature of a degenerate-box-only change.

Direct recomputation: 4 randomly selected pre-fix frames were re-encoded on GPU with the current code and compared to cache. Bit-exact on RoI features, scene tokens and boxes (max abs difference 0.00000).
verdict: Pre-fix cached rows reproduce exactly under current code. The mixed cache is sound; the completed runs are not affected by the incident.
scope_limit: Recomputation covered 4 frames, not all 81174 pre-fix files. Fingerprint verification covers all files for input/contract identity; recomputation confirms compute identity on a random sample.
run_provenance: All 12 runs of contextual-roi-20260917 started 15:56 EDT or later, after the 15:30-15:32 cache completion. No run used pre-fix code.
downstream: contextual-roi-all184-20260918 reuses this cache (no_new_encoder_extraction: true) and inherits this verified state.
actions_taken: Read-only verification. Nothing in the study directories was modified; recomputation wrote only to a scratch process.
